proposal.approach: Test a real three-level noncommuting pair using rational Taylor enclosures.
proposal.derivation: The strict upper endpoint must be negative to disprove the lower trace bound.
proposal.what_would_change: A strictly negative upper endpoint for the mean word trace minus the exponential trace on a valid pair disproves the lower bound.

math_review.hypotheses: The proposed pair is admissible. Both matrices are real symmetric, their maximum absolute row sums after division by 2 are 1, and (n,m)=(3,4) gives 35 words. Writing Δ for the mean word trace minus Tr exp(3H+4K), the proposed disproof requires Δ<0. The supplied execution reports a strictly positive lower endpoint. An independent exact calculation gives 26<Δ<27, ruling out this witness.
math_review.weakest_step: Candidate selection. Swapping H and K puts the three copies of exp(H) in the second-factor role, and the 3×3 first matrix has at most three eigenvalues. This falls within the stated public theorem. For the independent sign check, I replaced each exponential by its degree-32 Taylor polynomial and summed the 35 words by an integer recurrence with a common denominator. The rational polynomial gap lies between 26.68 and 26.69. Submultiplicativity and the geometric Taylor-tail bound give a total trace error below 10⁻⁷. The critical next test is an admissible noncommuting 4×4 pair with four distinct eigenvalues in each matrix and n=m=4. A strictly negative certified upper endpoint there would settle the universal question.

proposal.approach: No counterexample was found. With n=m=4, I first screened six pairs using a Hadamard change of eigenbasis. All six numerical gaps were positive. I then tested 256 pairs of a different form, setting K equal to −H plus a perturbation supported on a four-cycle. This cancels the diagonal of 4H+4K while preserving noncommutation. I certified the smallest numerical gap from the second search.
proposal.derivation: For this witness, the mean word trace minus Tr exp(4H+4K) lies strictly between 0.21227423577924 and 0.21227423577926. The four-cycle search varied the four edge magnitudes independently over {1,2,3,4}/16, with one edge negative. The selected pair has all four magnitudes equal to 1/16. Its maximum absolute row sums are 12/16 and 14/16. Both matrices have four distinct eigenvalues, since H is diagonal with distinct entries and the four Gershgorin intervals of K are disjoint. To certify the gap, I used the degree-32 exponential Taylor polynomial P and exact integer arithmetic with common denominator 16^32·32!. Starting from W(0,0)=I, I computed W(i,j)=P(H)W(i−1,j)+P(K)W(i,j−1), omitting terms with negative indices. Grouping words by first factor counts each of the 70 words once. For G=Tr W(4,4)/70−Tr P(4H+4K), exact division gave floor(10^14 G)=21227423577924. All three matrix arguments have infinity norm at most 1, so each exponential tail has norm below 2/33!, and each polynomial and exponential has norm below 3. Telescoping the eight factors and bounding the four-dimensional trace gives |Δ−G| < 4(1+8·3^7)·2/33! < 2·10^−32, where Δ is the true gap. This yields the stated interval.
proposal.what_would_change: A valid pair with a certified upper endpoint below zero would disprove the universal lower bound. The positive interval certifies the bound for this one pair. The other candidates were screened numerically, and the universal question remains open in this calculation.

math_review.hypotheses: The last pair is admissible. Both matrices are real symmetric, their maximum absolute row sums are 12/16 and 14/16, and n=m=4 gives 70 words. They do not commute because H has unequal first and second diagonal entries and K₁₂ is nonzero. H has four distinct eigenvalues. So does K, since the four Gershgorin intervals for 16K have centers −12, −4, 4, 12 and radius 2. For the mean word trace minus Tr exp(4H+4K), a strictly negative upper endpoint would disprove the universal bound. The executed checker instead gives a strictly positive lower endpoint.
math_review.weakest_step: Candidate selection. I independently replaced each exponential by its degree-32 Taylor polynomial and summed the 70 products by grouping words by first factor. For the resulting rational gap G, exact integer division gives floor(10¹⁸G)=212274235779246085. All three exponential arguments have infinity norm at most 1, so telescoping each eight-factor product bounds the total trace error by 4(1+8·3⁷)·2/33! < 2·10⁻³². Thus the true gap lies strictly between 0.21227423577924608 and 0.21227423577924609. This rules out the witness and leaves the universal question unresolved. The critical next test is to drop the search constraint diag(K)=−diag(H), vary the diagonal entries independently for admissible four-level pairs, and check any negative numerical gap for a strictly negative rational upper endpoint.

proposal.approach: No counterexample was found. I screened 512 four-dimensional pairs with independently sampled diagonals, diagonal H, and six signed off-diagonal entries in K. After all numerical gaps were positive, I screened 512 more pairs with H and K supported off the diagonal on two disjoint three-edge paths. I ranked candidates by the gap divided by Tr exp(nH+mK), which makes the ranking invariant under scalar shifts of either matrix. The witness below had the smallest relative gap across both screens, approximately 0.00092774.
proposal.derivation: For this pair, the true absolute gap Δ satisfies 0.705998593511 < Δ < 0.705998593514. Both matrices are symmetric, with maximum absolute row sums 4/16 and 21/16. They do not commute because H₁₁ differs from H₂₂ and K₁₂ is nonzero. To certify the gap, I used the degree-96 exponential Taylor polynomial P and exact integer arithmetic with common denominator 16⁹⁶·96! for each polynomial. Starting from W(0,0)=I, I computed W(i,j)=P(H)W(i−1,j)+P(K)W(i,j−1), taking terms with negative indices as zero. Grouping by first factor counts each of the 792 words once. For G=Tr W(5,7)/792−Tr P(5H+7K), exact division gave floor(10¹²G)=705998593512. The joint argument has infinity norm 152/16 < 10. For an argument of norm t≤10, the Taylor tail is bounded by 2t⁹⁷/97! by geometric summation. Each individual factor and its polynomial have norm below 8. Telescoping the twelve factors and using |Tr E|≤4‖E‖∞ gives |Δ−G|≤8(10⁹⁷+12·8¹¹·2⁹⁷)/97! < 10⁻⁵⁰, yielding the stated interval.
proposal.what_would_change: A valid pair with a certified gap upper endpoint below zero would disprove the universal lower bound. The rational interval establishes a strictly positive gap for this one witness. The other candidates received numerical screening only. The universal question remains unresolved by this calculation.
